guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 for applications that integrate with customer accounts. For read-only issue title access in each connected person's workspace, the least-privilege documented grant is the default read scope, which is always present. Registration, the authorization redirect, and token exchange are setup requirements. Pagination uses documented cursor arguments on the GraphQL API. Write scopes are not needed and should not be requested. Distribution requirements for other customer workspaces are not in the supplied snapshots.

findings.detail: Linear supports OAuth2 for applications integrating with Linear. The authorization request requires client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and a scope list. findings.title: Use the default read scope for read-only issue access
findings.detail: The read scope gives read access for the authorizing user's account and is always present. It is the documented minimum for reading issue titles. It does not grant issues:create or write access.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles
steps.detail: Call the GraphQL endpoint with the Bearer access token and query the first 10 issues with title and pageInfo. The response issues.nodes array delivers the title values in each node, and pageInfo.hasNextPage and pageInfo.endCursor control continuation. Expected output is a JSON data.issues object with nodes containing title strings.
steps.doneWhen: The response has data.issues.nodes with title values and a pageInfo object containing hasNextPage and endCursor. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: ```graphql query Issues {
} ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query { issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response for the connected person
title: field on each issue node in data.issues.nodes
pageInfo.hasNextPage and pageInfo.endCursor: used for the next request

steps.title: Read the next page of issue titles using endCursor
steps.detail: Repeat the query with the after argument set to pageInfo.endCursor from the previous response. Continue while hasNextPage is true. Stop when hasNextPage is false. Each page's nodes add title values to the listing. Keep repeating the first-argument-after-cursor query with the latest endCursor until pageInfo.hasNextPage returns false. The documented end condition is hasNextPage false.
steps.doneWhen: The continuation response returns further issue nodes and pageInfo.hasNextPage is false when the listing ends. A response returns pageInfo.hasNextPage false and all pages have been read. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
